feedback:
Written before this candidate races, so it states no result for it. The candidate is iteration 7 (score 425.8, best so far) with one change: kd 1.0 to 1.2. Iteration 7 showed that kd 0.8 to 1.0 and the sensor move to y=0.06 improved s-bend progress (0.46 to 0.61) while the oval stayed at 20/20 (iteration 7 oval: finish 1.0, mean time 1.74 s, max_error 0.021, steering_oscillation 0.197). Iteration 4 (kp 5.5, speed 1.05, kd 1.0) cut the oval to 13/20, so its oval damage came from kp and speed, not kd. The effect of kd alone above 1.0 is untested, which is why one field is the right size for this step. The candidate is valid and inside every contract limit, and the kp, ki, base_speed, sensor layout, wheel track and mass are all unchanged from the best raced design. Its only risk is that higher kd amplifies sensor noise, which would show up as higher steering_oscillation.

After the race, read the results in this order. (a) If the oval stays at 20/20 with steering_oscillation at or below about 0.3 and s-bend progress rises above 0.7 with line_loss_events below 1, keep kd 1.2 and test kd 1.4 next, since damping is the lever that has helped on bends. (b) If steering_oscillation on the oval rises above about 0.3, or the oval finish drops below 1.0, revert kd to 1.0 and keep y 0.06, because the extra derivative is amplifying noise. (c) If s-bend progress is flat (within about 0.05 of 0.61) while the oval holds, damping is no longer the limit. Return to kd 1.0 and try wheel_track 0.09 alone, since iterations 1 to 3 showed that a narrower track raised bend progress without losing the oval. Iteration 5 showed that wheel_track 0.09 combined with mass 0.5 cut the oval to 25%, so keep mass at 0.6.
requested_changes: If the oval holds at 20/20 with steering_oscillation at or below about 0.3 and s-bend progress above 0.7 with line_loss_events below 1: keep kd 1.2 and try kd 1.4 next, since kd alone (iteration 7 vs 3) improved s-bend progress without losing the oval.

If oval steering_oscillation rises above about 0.3 or the oval finish drops below 1.0: revert kd to 1.0 and keep y 0.06, because higher derivative gain amplifies sensor noise, and iteration 4 showed that kp 5.5 and speed 1.05 are the costly changes, so do not raise kp.

If s-bend progress stays flat near 0.61 with the oval holding: return kd to 1.0 and test wheel_track 0.09 alone with mass 0.6, because iterations 1 to 3 showed a narrower track raised bend progress without losing the oval, and iteration 5 showed that the mass change was part of its oval loss.
